papers.title: Protocol-aware dual-view single-channel EEG sleep staging with improved N1 discrimination on public sleep-EDF and SHHS benchmarks.
papers.summary: Developed DualViewSeqSleepNet, a protocol-aware single-channel EEG sleep-staging model combining waveform and spectral encoders with cross-epoch aggregation and N1-aware supervision. On Sleep-EDF it reached macro-F1 0.821 and accuracy 0.869, raising N1 F1 from 0.506 to 0.535, and achieved macro-F1 0.791 on SHHS-1 without retuning.

papers.title: MLE EEG Toolbox: A Personal AI Laboratory Assistant for Literature-Informed and Reproducible M/EEG Research
papers.summary: Introduced MLE EEG Toolbox, a locally deployed AI assistant framework that translates natural-language instructions into researcher-approved M/EEG analysis operations, integrating literature retrieval, parameter guidance, and replayable computational provenance. It reported action-selection accuracies of 85.6% for EEG and 95.5% for MEG, with 142 cross-platform tests showing close numerical agreement and demonstrated spectral, network, decoding, and source analyses on public datasets.

papers.title: From clusters to curves: A model-based alternative to cluster-based permutation tests for the analysis of time-resolved data
papers.summary: Proposed a model-based alternative to cluster-based permutation testing for M/EEG time-resolved data using Bayesian generalized additive multilevel models that yield posterior odds at each time point while accounting for between-participant variability. Simulations recovered effect onset and extent accurately across signal-to-noise ratios, and an empirical MEG decoding dataset showed the highest split-half temporal overlap among compared methods.

papers.title: Hidden Drowsiness in Wakefulness: Differences in Resting-State EEG Profiles in Natural Short Sleepers Versus Recommended Length Sleepers.
papers.summary: Compared resting-state eyes-open EEG in natural short sleepers versus recommended-length sleepers, finding higher global alpha power and regionally steeper aperiodic exponents (especially occipital) in natural short sleepers, both markers of increased drowsiness. A Group × Region interaction and a trend toward increasing aperiodic exponents over time suggested less stable wakefulness under low stimulation.

papers.title: Directional brain-heart interaction during cognitive workload: a permutation conditional mutual information approach.
papers.summary: Applied Permutation Conditional Mutual Information (PCMI) to characterize directional brain-heart interaction, first validating it on synthetic coupled time series and then on simultaneous EEG-ECG recordings during baseline and mental arithmetic in 36 subjects. Brain-heart interaction complexity increased during mental arithmetic, mainly involving anterior and posterior scalp regions and vagal- and sympathovagal-related HRV components.

papers.title: NeuroSim: a clinically informed multi-disorder EEG simulator with personalized pattern injection and AI-driven neurological modeling
papers.summary: Presents NeuroSim, an open-source framework generating synthetic multichannel EEG with user-controlled injection of disease-specific spectral patterns across five disorders and severity levels, reproducing expected biomarkers. A convolutional-attention classifier trained on simulated data reached 95.3–96.8% hold-out accuracy, and augmenting real clinical EEG with NeuroSim samples improved AD vs. control accuracy from 91.6% to 94.5% and PD vs. control from 90.9% to 94.0%.

papers.title: SafeLens: A Statistically Controlled Nonlinear Machine Learning Framework for Characterizing Hidden Dynamics in Event-Locked Neural Activity.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduces SafeLens, a sliding-window random-forest framework with empirical null sampling that maps nonlinear reliance on multiscale temporal derivatives across time-frequency space while controlling family-wise error. On simulated cortico-cortical evoked potentials injected into resting intracranial EEG, it recovered ~2.5 times more polarity-resolved deflections with ~5–11 times fewer false components, and in eight patients detected CCEPs until 1,040 ms post-stimulation versus 570 and 455 ms for benchmarks.

papers.title: Seizure Prediction Using Channel-Optimized Intracranial EEG With Variable Interictal and Preictal Durations.
papers.journal: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
papers.summary: Evaluated seizure prediction on long-term SWEC-ETHZ intracranial EEG across six interictal (24/48 h) and preictal (30/60/90 min) duration combinations, comparing all-channel, single-channel majority voting, and channel-optimization majority voting strategies. Channel optimization performed best in every combination, reaching up to 87.7% sensitivity, 94.6% specificity, 0.912 AUC at the segment level and 95.9% sensitivity with 0.05/h FPR at the event level, forecasting seizures up to 90 min ahead.

papers.title: A shared slowing axis and phenotype-specific rhythms link clinical EEG to FDG-PET dementia phenotypes.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Applied nonnegative tensor decomposition to clinical EEG in 455 patients, deriving six latent factors and relating them to FDG-PET-defined neurodegenerative phenotypes, regional metabolism, and cognition. Four oscillatory factors (posterior alpha, Rolandic beta, frontotemporal delta-theta, posterior theta-slow alpha) varied across phenotypes, with posterior theta-slow alpha becoming more phenotype-specific after slowing adjustment (eta-squared 0.082 to 0.147), and a four-factor logistic classifier separated cognitively unimpaired participants from DLB, posterior cortical atrophy, and AD variants with AUC > 0.8.

papers.title: FUSE: FUsing EEG-MEG in a Shared Embedding via self-supervised learning for BCI
papers.summary: Introduces FUSE, a two-phase self-supervised framework that learns a shared EEG-MEG latent representation by predicting power spectral density from time-domain activity and then reuses the frozen encoder for motor imagery BCI classification. On simultaneous EEG-MEG from 20 participants, the learned representations raised median accuracy from 0.734 with handcrafted spectral features to 0.794, also outperforming MEG alone (0.680) and slightly EEG alone (0.765), with cross-subject transfer within 0.01 accuracy for over half of models.

papers.title: The Potency Stability Tradeoff: Evaluating EEG Biomarkers for Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.summary: Deconstructed EEG-based MDD biomarkers using connectivity, spectral, and complexity features from 30 MDD patients and 88 controls under leakage-free cross-validation, finding Theta-Alpha signals maximally predictive (AUC 0.683) but unstable (Jaccard 0.187), while stability-optimized consensus feature selection gave superior generalization (AUC 0.792 vs 0.662). Concludes biomarker stability matters more than signal strength for clinically reliable diagnostics.

papers.title: Intrarater reliability of expert electroencephalographic interpretation of 100 full-length recordings.
papers.summary: Conducted a 'noise audit' in which 14 expert epileptologists independently rated the same 100 full-length EEGs on two occasions at least 60 days apart to measure intrarater reliability. Percent self-agreement ranged from 96% for generalized epileptiform to 82% for any nonepileptiform abnormality, with strong correlation to interrater agreement, though flipped decisions were frequent enough to be clinically consequential.

papers.title: Frontotemporal Slow-Frequency Dominance in Quantitative EEG as a Potential Biomarker of Post-COVID Cognitive Dysfunction.
authors: María Mar González Álvarez de Sotomayor
papers.summary: Exploratory case-control qEEG study of 21 patients with persistent cognitive complaints after mild COVID-19 versus 21 matched controls found a spatially heterogeneous shift toward slower spectral activity, most consistent in frontal and right temporal electrodes, with modest cognitive associations and exploratory classification performance (ROC-AUC up to 0.949). Findings require confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

papers.title: Next generation Human Neocortical Neurosolver model with biophysically realistic somatic, dendritic and synaptic dynamics.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Presents a significantly updated Human Neocortical Neurosolver model with electrophysiological properties and synaptic connections tuned to human tissue, including L5 dendritic Ca2+ spikes and shorter L2/3 dendritic spikes, plus software workflows and tutorials for disentangling somatic, synaptic, and dendritic contributions to EEG/MEG signatures.

papers.title: Altered oscillatory coupling and a candidate inhibitory circuit mechanism in Rett syndrome
papers.summary: Combined resting-state EEG from 42 RTT individuals and 37 controls with biophysically constrained Layer 4 network modeling and found elevated phase-amplitude coupling (e.g., theta-gamma and alpha-gamma) in RTT; simulations showed that reduced VIP+ interneuron excitability selectively reproduced the increased coupling.

papers.title: A report-supervised EEG-language foundation model enables broad, interactive clinical interpretation
papers.summary: Introduces EEG Copilot, a biosignal-language foundation model trained on routine EEG-report pairs without task-specific expert labels. Across external datasets it matched an expert-supervised model on 11 findings (mean AUROC 0.80–0.81), assessed 23 clinical characteristics via natural-language queries in English and German, and produced clinically usable integrated impressions.

papers.title: False-Positive Calls of Reimplemented Published Analyses for Covert Command-Following on Electroencephalograms Recorded Without Study Commands.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Applied 11 reimplemented published EEG analyses for covert command-following to recordings made without commands across large clinical cohorts, measuring false-positive rates. Three of ten analyses called significantly more than 5% of patients positive (up to 23.3%, and 11.5–27.3% after cardiac arrest) while still detecting genuine responses, and the authors identify variance handling, configuration/time selection, and permissive thresholds as contributors.

papers.title: Video-Based Automated Seizure Classification Using Multimodal Large Language Models.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: Developed a multimodal large language model framework to extract semiological features from 90 seizure videos and classify epileptic versus nonepileptic seizures; MLLM-extracted features with a KNN classifier achieved F1=0.76 and AUC=0.76, correctly identifying 68/90 events.

papers.title: Neuromodulation of cortical networks facilitates motor generalization of balance training in older adults.
papers.summary: Randomized 40 older adults to tVNS or sham during stabilometer balance training and found that tVNS produced greater improvements in center-of-pressure area and changes in postural dynamics, with beta-band EEG minimum spanning tree changes (increased leaf fraction, reduced eccentricity/diameter) suggesting cortical network reorganization.

papers.title: Electric and Magnetic Source Imaging in Epilepsy: Anatomical Insights from Realistic Simulations.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Used realistic simulations with known ground truth to compare HD-EEG and MEG spike detectability and ESI/MSI/EMSI localization for epileptogenic sources; EEG detected more radial gyral/sulcal-bottom sources while MEG detected more tangential sulcal-wall sources, and MSI localized tangential sources more accurately than ESI.

papers.title: A Soft Sponge-Pillar Electrode Platform for Motion-Tolerant Ambulatory EEG and Sleep Monitoring.
papers.summary: A soft sponge-pillar EEG electrode of two-layer carbon black-PDMS composite, fabricated by sugar templating, was developed for motion-tolerant ambulatory recording, achieving contact impedance of 1.62×10^4 Ω at 10 Hz and maintaining gel stability over 18 hours. Integrated into headbands, headphones, and caps, it recorded EEG during motion with 16.46 dB SNR, supporting wearable long-term EEG and sleep monitoring.

papers.title: Temporal dissociation across the eye-brain-muscle cascade delineates a preparation window before muscle activation in subacute stroke.
papers.summary: Recorded eye-tracking, EEG, and EMG synchronously in 30 subacute stroke survivors and 30 controls during a nine-grid reaching task, showing stepwise delays in visual engagement and muscle activation bracketing a cortical preparation window; gaze-timing features classified reaching action occurrence with AUC 0.973 and accuracy 0.918.

papers.title: TGAN-TSR: A type-aware graph attention time-spectral representation for heterogeneous fusion networks in gear system fault diagnosis.
papers.summary: Proposes TGAN-TSR, a type-aware graph attention network that fuses temporal and spectral (including higher-order spectral coupling) features via a dual-channel extractor and graph-based type-aware fusion for gear system fault diagnosis. On public benchmarks and a proprietary gearbox dataset it significantly improved diagnostic accuracy and captured key fault signatures.

papers.title: What's in a Story? Studying Neural Narrative Engagement with Auditory Passages Using EEG Inter-Subject Correlation
papers.summary: Used EEG inter-subject correlation (ISC) in 46 adults listening to social and non-social narrated excerpts and found no significant relationship with broad social/non-social categories, but ISC for high sociocognitive word usage significantly exceeded medium and low usage in reliable component RC3. Summed ratings of interest, compulsion, and enjoyment positively correlated with ISC in RC2 and across RC1–RC3, suggesting independent additive effects of passage content and behavioral responses.

papers.title: Group-specific associations among sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and frontal alpha asymmetry in college students: evidence from a cross-sectional EEG study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 120 college students (60 with elevated depressive symptoms, 60 controls), the depressive-symptom group had higher PSQI scores and lower composite frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA). PSQI correlated positively with depressive symptoms in both groups, while FAA correlated negatively with PSQI and depressive symptoms only in the depressive-symptom group, where PSQI and FAA jointly explained depressive symptom severity (R²=0.243).

papers.title: Evaluation of Antiseizure Potential of Rufinamide and Celecoxib Combination in a PTZ-Kindled Mouse Model Through Electrophysiological, Neurobehavioral, and Molecular Analyses.
papers.summary: Tested rufinamide and celecoxib, alone and combined, during PTZ-kindling in mice, assessing seizures (behavioral scoring, EEG), cognition/anxiety/depression behaviors, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation. Rufinamide alone and the RUF+CEL combination reduced seizure progression and epileptiform discharges and improved neurobehavioral, biochemical, and hippocampal histopathological outcomes.

papers.title: Electrophysiology of multisite direct electrical stimulation in the human brain.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In 20 participants with stereo-EEG, simultaneous multisite direct electrical stimulation showed that synchronized dual-site stimulation engaged a larger effective network than single-site stimulation; linear superposition explained most responses, with sublinear (saturation) responses proximal to stimulation sites and supralinear late responses at network-connected sites. Low-intensity dual-site stimulation matched or exceeded higher-intensity single-site stimulation, and these principles extended to three-site stimulation.

papers.title: A high-throughput all-optical platform for mapping gene perturbations to electrophysiology.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Develops a high-throughput all-optical electrophysiology platform combining an engineered hiPSC line (inducible NGN2, CRISPRi, Voltron2/CheRiff), wide-field voltage imaging, and automated analysis, recording ~1,500 spiking neurons at 800 Hz. Arrayed knockdown of five sodium/potassium channel genes produced distinct electrophysiological phenotypes, supporting scalable functional genomics.

papers.title: Frontal Low-Frequency Electroencephalographic Coherence in Bipolar Disorder: A Covariate-Controlled Secondary Analysis of a Public Resting-State EEG Feature Dataset.
papers.summary: In a covariate-controlled secondary analysis of a public resting-state EEG dataset (93 healthy controls, 66 bipolar disorder, 196 depressive disorder, 117 schizophrenia), bipolar disorder showed higher adjusted frontal/frontopolar delta, theta, and combined delta-theta coherence than all comparison groups, with effects strongest in frontopolar electrode pairs. Differences from depressive disorder and schizophrenia were smaller and concentrated in frontopolar pairs susceptible to ocular artifacts, so the findings do not establish a diagnostic biomarker or source-level mechanism.

papers.title: Aesthetic preference for the visual appearance of modern decorative cabinets in young adults: An ERP study.
papers.summary: Recorded EEG/ERPs in 31 young adults rating modern decorative cabinet images alongside CAPS affective pictures to examine neural correlates of aesthetic preference. Medium-preference cabinets elicited larger frontal N100 amplitudes than high- or low-preference images, while LPP did not differ across cabinet preference levels, implicating early perceptual processing.

papers.title: Clinical outcomes and EEG monitoring in absence epilepsy trials: A narrative review.
papers.summary: Narrative review of EEG-monitored generalized spike-and-wave (GSW) as an outcome measure in absence epilepsy trials, reporting that nearly 100% of clinical absence seizures show sustained GSW, >49% of electrographic seizures are asymptomatic, and antiseizure medications effective in absence epilepsy reduce GSW. Recommends incorporating ≥24-h EEG monitoring and comorbidity outcomes in future trials.

papers.title: Depressive symptoms moderate daily anticipated and momentary emotion dynamics and associate with complex brain network topology: Resting-state EEG and ecological momentary assessment evidence.
papers.summary: Combining resting-state EEG minimum spanning tree analysis with 14-day ecological momentary assessment (3 assessments/day) in 96 young adults, the study found anticipated emotion prospectively predicted subsequent momentary positive and negative emotion, but this link attenuated to non-significance beyond PHQ-9 scores of 5.7-9.7. Theta- and delta-band topological metrics were indirectly associated with daily emotional dynamics via baseline depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Rituximab-responsive epilepsia partialis continua in autoimmune Polyendocrine syndrome: A video-EEG-EMG polygraphic study.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: Video-EEG-EMG polygraphic case report of a 54-year-old woman with autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome presenting with epilepsia partialis continua (EPC) of the right fingers; ictal SPECT showed left hand-knob hyperperfusion and EEG-EMG showed left central spikes preceding EMG bursts by 30–40 ms. Rituximab produced complete, sustained clinical and electrophysiological remission at 18-month follow-up after corticosteroids, IVIG, and antiseizure medications failed.

papers.title: Nonverbal reasoning in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy: associations with gross motor function, MRI, and EEG findings.
papers.journal: Child neuropsychology : a journal on normal and abnormal development in childhood and adolescence
papers.summary: Multicenter cross-sectional study of 40 children/adolescents with cerebral palsy and 20 comparison participants examining nonverbal reasoning (Raven CPM) in relation to GMFCS level, MRI, and EEG findings. CPM scores were markedly lower in CP (median 72 vs 98), showed a strong inverse association with GMFCS level, and were lower with predominant white matter injury.

papers.title: Safety, Signal Quality, and Patient Satisfaction With Insertable Loop Recorder Implantation by Specialized Electrophysiology Nurses: Prospective Observational Study.
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study of 35 patients, specialized electrophysiology nurses implanted insertable loop recorders with no procedural complications, a mean signal amplitude of 0.45 mV and visible P waves in 94.3%, and high patient satisfaction (97.1% maximum or very high).

papers.title: Multimodal characterization of putative pan -inhibitory viral constructs in macaque monkeys.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The study characterized three Dlx5-6-based pan-inhibitory viral vectors in seven rhesus macaques using in vivo and in vitro electrophysiology and immunohistochemistry, finding reliable inhibitory neuron targeting (81-97% specificity) but incomplete coverage (32-64% of GABAergic neurons), with subtype biases and construct-dependent efficacy for optotagging and suppression.

papers.title: Human herpesvirus 7-associated encephalitis diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing in pediatric patients: a retrospective study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective study of 16 immunocompetent children with HHV-7-associated encephalitis diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing, most presented with fever, headache, and vomiting, and although generally having a favorable prognosis, unfavorable outcomes occurred in three patients including one death.

papers.title: Norepinephrine inhibits Afferent activation of NTS Catecholamine Neurons in Mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using patch-clamp electrophysiology in mouse brainstem slices, the study found that norepinephrine inhibits solitary tract afferent-evoked excitatory postsynaptic currents onto NTS catecholamine neurons via presynaptic α2-adrenergic receptors, and that neuropeptide Y acts similarly through Y2 receptors with additive or synergistic effects.

papers.title: Gut microbiota‑driven indole‑3‑propionic acid protects against sepsis‑associated encephalopathy via inhibiting BNIP3L ubiquitination and restoring BNIP3L‑dependent mitophagy as a potential molecular mechanism.
papers.summary: In mouse models and a clinical cohort, gut microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) was depleted in sepsis-associated encephalopathy, and IPA supplementation improved survival, cognition, mitochondrial function, and reduced neuroinflammation, with plasma IPA showing diagnostic value (AUC 0.891); mechanistic evidence suggested a correlative link to BNIP3L ubiquitination and mitophagy, though direct BNIP3L-specific ubiquitination was not confirmed.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning for infrared spectral analysis of bone.
papers.summary: Using optical photothermal infrared spectroscopy of wild-type and osteogenesis imperfecta mouse bone, full-spectrum fingerprint-region (1800-800 cm-1) models reached 87-90% phenotype classification accuracy versus 59-63% for conventional peak-ratio parameters, with similar performance across PLS-DA, logistic regression, and XGBoost. SHAP and VIP identified prominent contributions from collagen-associated Amide I and II regions.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
